Answer: A
Reason: The chest radiograph demonstrates multiple bilateral pulmonary nodules, some of which appear to have central lucency or cavitation (particularly in the right mid-zone and left upper zone), a hallmark finding for septic pulmonary emboli. This presentation of multifocal cavitating nodules distinguishes it from simple effusions, edema, or typical metastases which rarely cavitate in this manner without other primary history.
